articles.title: Planned asylum seeker detention centre next to Oxfordshire sewage works criticised
articles.summary:
Thames Water says detainees at proposed accommodation should expect to experience insect swarms and strong smells

A Home Office plan to build asylum seeker detention facilities next to a…

blocks.text: A Home Office plan to build asylum seeker detention facilities next to a sewage pump is facing objections after water company officials warned that detainees should expect to experience insect swarms and strong smells.

Proposed secure accommodation blocks at Campsfield House immigration removal centre in Oxfordshire will be 20 metres from a sewage pumping station, according to a written submission from Thames Water.

A senior development manager at the company wrote that it could give rise to “amenity effects, including odour, noise, vibration, lighting associated with maintenance activities, insects and flies” for any inhabitants. In a previous submission, the company wrote that any development may lead to sewage flooding.
The warnings, which come as the government hopes to expand the immigration detention estate by 40%, have been seized upon by campaigners against the expansion.

Ally Swadling, the lead legal education officer at the charity Right to Remain, said: “Thames Water’s concerns about sewage infrastructure at Campsfield show how little regard is being given to even the most basic standards of sanitation and human dignity.
“They reinforce what we already know – this government is putting its political priorities above people’s lives and wellbeing.”
The centre near Kidlington re-opened in December 2025 after it was shut in 2018 following years of problems, including suicides, riots, escapes and complaints about conditions.

The Home Office is planning to increase the centre’s capacity from 160 bed spaces to 400, and to convert existing buildings. According to the Thames Water submission in October, officials also “raised concerns regarding capacity within the foul water, surface water and water supply networks” in the local area.
A separate 2015 written consultation response, which was submitted in June, states the development may lead to sewage flooding in the area.

“Thames Water request that an impact study be undertaken to ascertain, with a greater degree of certainty, whether the proposed development will lead to overloading of existing infrastructure,” it said.
Written representations, including that of Thames Water, will be heard at a public inquiry beginning on 14 December.
Oxfordshire county council has formally objected to the expansion of Campsfield House, saying it risks intensifying existing public concern, and called for the site to be shut permanently.
after newsletter promotion
According to the Home Office, nearly 80,000 people have been returned or deported from the UK since the 2024 election to the end of June 2026, an increase of 52% on the previous two years.

Imran Hussain, the director of external affairs at the Refugee Council, said: “Detention is a harmful, dehumanising experience that must only be used as a last resort. Evidence shows it’s ineffective, expensive and damages people forced to endure it.

“Instead of expanding sites such as Campsfield House immigration removal centre, and in this case, in a way that could potentially be detrimental to the health and wellbeing of people staying there, the government must instead use community-based alternatives detention, which have proven to be effective and much cheaper.”

A spokesperson for the Home Office said: “We are confident in our plans for Campsfield immigration removal centre and will continue to engage constructively with the Planning Inspectorate as the process moves forward. We are committed to increasing the removal of those with no right to remain in the UK. Expanding our detention capacity plays an important role in achieving this.”
Thames Water said they had nothing to add to their response.

articles.title: Cape Verde goes to the polls in presidential vote
articles.summary: Known for its political stability and good governance, the island nation will vote for its next president. About 420,000 people are eligible to vote

image.caption: Cape Verde went to the polls to vote for its next presidentImage: Danilson Sequeira/REUTERS

blocks.text: Elections in Cape Verdefor the country's next president took place on Sunday.

The two main candidates are current leader 66-year-old Jose Maria Neves, considered the favorite of winning a second term, and Joana Rosa Amando, 61, a former justice minister who could become the country's first-ever female president. Four other candidates take part in the race.
Each of the top candidates has the support of one of the country's two main parties.
According to Amandu, a woman winning the presidential race would show many young women and girls that "no government job is barred from them."

blocks.caption: President Jose Maria Neves is considered the favorite for winning a second termImage: Danilson Sequeira/REUTERS

blocks.text: Results expected during night
Voting started at 09:00 GMT and will end at 19:00 GMT in the west Africanarchipelago. Provisional results are expected during the night.
Some 420,000 people are eligible to vote, with the election being watched by about 150 observers from the Economic Community of West African States, the African Union and European Union.
The country is made of ten volcanic islands, is located in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometers (375 miles) off the coast of Senegal.
Good governance

Cape Verde is known for its democratic stability and good governance, and its economy has been showing strong growth. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's 2026 index on global governance has the country in third place of Africa's 54 countries, with only Seychellesand Mauritius faring better.

blocks.caption: Joana Rosa could become Cape Verde's first female presidentImage: Danilson Sequeira/REUTERS

blocks.text: Its political system is semi-presidential, with the prime minister being responsible for the executive. The president, in turn, is responsible for guaranteeing unity and upholding the constitution.
According to the World Bank, Cape Verde is an upper-middle-income country due to its growing tourism industry.
The challenges it faces range from social inequality, the islands' geographic isolation and the lack of traveling options between islands.
The increased cost of living, energy prices and youth unemployment also play a role.

The country became world renowned after its national team reached the 2026 World Cup's knockout stages despite taking part in it for the first time. Goalkeeper Vozinha, 40, became a world star due to his performance against later world champions Spain.

articles.title: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
articles.summary: Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the coalition government insists broadcasters need to cut costs.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Czech radio said it's the largest protest in the history of the independent Czech Republic
Thousands of people have gathered in central Prague to protest against the Czech government's plans to scrap the license fee and use the state budget to fund public media.
Critics say the plans would allow politicians to stifle media freedom.

The coalition government - which consists of the populist ANO party and two right-wing Eurosceptic parties - insists the change will not affect editorial independence, but wants broadcasters to cut costs.
Parliament passed the first draft of the proposal late last month. Since then, thousands of Czechs have taken part in protests.
Czech households currently pay ⁠205 crowns ($9.44, £7.06) a month for Czech TV and Czech radio.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Organisers say the protest in Prague's Letna park has "roughly 400,000" attendees, making it the largest protest since the country's independence in 1993

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Organisers say the protest in Prague's Letna park has "roughly 400,000" attendees, making it the largest protest since the country's independence in 1993
Sunday's protest was organised by the Million Moments for Democracy association which said "roughly 400,000" people had attended.
It is being described as the largest protest since the Czech Republic's independence in 1993.
"I know that our entire Czech Television is a guarantee of truth and objectivity," pensioner Milana Rudolfova, 72, told Reuters news agency.
"If we do not have public television and radio then unfortunately we will not be able to believe anything anymore."

blocks.caption: Two young people wear paper hats while holding a huge EU flag

blocks.text: Some protesters wore pointed hats folded out of newspapers as a tribute to an animated character, Večerníček, who has introduced Czech Television's nightly children's bedtime stories for decades.
Critics have compared the government's media bill to changes in Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who tightly controlled state media when he was in power.
Prime Minister Andrej Babis was appointed in December in 2025, and has faced criticism over his coalition's attacks on Czech media.

"Political attacks against private and public media have become one of the hallmarks of Andrej Babis' premiership," said Pavol Szalai, Prague Bureau director of international press freedom organisation Reporters Without Borders, in June.

articles.title: Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage
articles.summary:
Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration hasn’t properly invested existing funds

Donald Trump’s…

blocks.text: Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a lack of congressional funding – though a Democratic senator argued that the Trump administration hasn’t properly invested all of the funds it has already been given to implement needed air travel infrastructure upgrades.

“I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash, a day after he said routine but necessary maintenance botched by a contractor had caused Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop, leading to the delay or cancellation of thousands of flights.
Meanwhile, Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland criticized how the Trump administration has managed existing funding allocated for the improvements coveted by Duffy.

“It’s really rich to hear the secretary pointing the fingers at Congress when Congress has given the administration what they asked for,” Van Hollen separately told CNN’s Bash on Sunday morning. “If they need more, they should come up and justify it. I will support what is necessary to have a safe system and a reliable system.”
Duffy claimed the congressional funding which Van Hollen mentioned – $12.5bn – was limited in scope and not nearly enough.

“I have no money in that $12.5bn that I can use for a new architecture for telecom,” said Duffy. “I can’t build new software to manage our airplanes in the airspace because it dates back to the 1990s, but there’s no money for that. There’s no money for towers. Our towers are old.”
Duffy also spent part of the interview with CNN defending Trump, who waited until Sunday to remark on the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.

The president’s comments came in the form of social media posts blaming the Biden administration and describing himself as busy “in the White House having meetings on many subjects”. They came after he had posted about what he envisioned to be a bipartisan congressional initiative to revitalize the motion picture and television industries.

“Before I even was sworn in, the president who loves the airspace was telling me we have to modernize,” Duffy said to Bash. “This is the first president we have who cares this much about modernizing the airspace.”
When asked why Trump took two days to comment on the ground stop, Duffy claimed he was in constant behind-the-scene contact with the president.
“He was fully engaged because this is important to him, and it’s important to America,” Duffy claimed. “The president is fully supportive, fully engaged, and was fully tracking what’s happening.”
In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump blamed Joe Biden and demanded funding from Congress.

“The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad,” Trump wrote. “We have the knowledge and plan for the Flight Control Systems, we need Congress to give the money, FAST!”

In another interview on Sunday on CBS News’ Face the Nation, Duffy told host Margaret Brennan that the FAA was currently investigating the root cause of the botched maintenance work that triggered the ground stop. He said the maintenance involved – replacing telecommunication lines from old copper wire to fiber optic cables – has occurred “thousands of times” without any issues.

The contractor, L3Harris, is reportedly conducting diagnostics testing. Duffy, as he has repeatedly done, said there continued being no indication of a foreign cyberattack. Professional Aviation Safety Specialists (Pass), the AFL-CIO labor union representing more than 11,000 workers at the FAA, said technicians it represents were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop.

“The issue was isolated to two contractor owned and maintained routers that were being updated midday,” the union said in a statement. “Historically, contractors have followed a protocol where FAA employees conduct a risk assessment and coordinate the maintenance of the system or equipment.”
But the union said Pass-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades at the center of Friday’s ground stop.
Duffy told Brennan in response to the union’s statement that “this was done appropriately, which by the way, it’s been done thousands of times by us, by others, by other companies”.

“This has never happened,” Duffy argued. “That’s why when you have a remote location like this, we felt comfortable doing it in the middle of the day because it’s been done thousands of times. We’ve never had this situation. We’re going to have to re-evaluate when we do this work.”
When asked if a risk assessment was conducted, Duffy did not directly answer. He said: “We do risk assessments on everything.”
Duffy also cited a Government Accountability Office report published in September 2026 that noted the need to modernize air traffic control systems.

He was asked about the report noting that “it could be prioritizing speed over costs and air traffic disruptions” in implementing a modernization effort of air traffic control systems. Duffy claimed, “In regard to speed, we are going, I think … at that the right speed.”

Pass has also called for progress on improving staffing of certified professional technicians at the FAA – and for the union to be fully engaged in efforts to implement what has been dubbed the Brand New Air Traffic Control System.
“These employees should receive training on new equipment and could ensure more robust installation and optimization – if the workforce were properly staffed,” the union added.

articles.title: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?
articles.summary: The German economy is growing again, albeit slightly. However, economists warn that without reforms, higher productivity and solid public finances, a loss of prosperity and growing debt threaten…

image.caption: Experts predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027, but it's not enough for Germany's ageing societyImage: Michael Probst/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Is Germany's economy back on the up? The answer to that question depends on your perspective.

At the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen. "A year ago, I said here: We are angry. Today I must say: We are stunned," Bertram Kawlath, president of the Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA), said in his opening remarks on Tuesday.

The mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades. It once employed more than a million people; now 15,000 positions are being cut every month. Production has shrunk about 20% since 2018.
Kawlath criticized the federal government's infighting and lack of reform, as well as what the companies consider a continued high bureaucracy and tax burden.
"[We are] stunned by the whitewashing in so many government statements. Stunned by the increasingly visible decline of our country as a business location."
Germany's economy is growing again — a little
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised quick reforms and a rapidly noticeable economic upswing when he took office in May 2025. A year and a half later, reality has caught up with him.

Merz's coalition of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union, (CSU), along with the center-left Social Democrats(SPD), keeps running into trouble. In addition, there are crises and wars. The German economy is facing more headwinds than seldom before, Merz said in October at the German Employers' Day conference in Berlin.

blocks.caption: Earlier this week, economic experts gave Chancellor Friedrich Merz their  2026 report — and words of cautionImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Given the circumstances, small successes are even more meaningful. "A heartfelt thanks for the good news you bring," Merz said when he received the autumn report of the Council of Economic Experts in Berlin, which predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027.
The economic experts have a German government mandate to independently analyze business activity and make recommendations for economic policy. Earlier this year, they were much more pessimistic.

"The German economy has recovered quicker than expected from the energy price shock sparked by the war in Iran," said Monika Schnitzer, chair of the expert advisory board, explaining the prognosis. "We see a significant economic recovery, driven by surprisingly strong exports and high government spending."

The chancellor, who celebrated his 71st birthday on November 11, spoke of "encouraging signals" in his address. "The economy in Germany is slowly on the rise again. Considering the many crises in Germany, it was not totally expected that we would manage that."
Why 1% growth is not enough
But these improved prospects do not change the long-term problems. An ageing society means the bills for pensions, health and caregiving are constantly rising.

At the same time, the number of working-age people who finance these services is sinking. That puts increasing pressure on the public purse. According to Berlin's financial planning, social welfare costs, defense and interest on debt will account for 80% of the spending in the federal government's budget.
What are the German government's pension, labor reforms?

"We must realize that in the long term the expected revenues in the federal budget will not be enough to cover the planned expenses," Schnitzer warned. The growth rates are far below what is needed to secure the same level of prosperity as previous decades in the long term.
"To grow out of this budgetary predicament, we would need levels of economic growth which we haven't experienced in Germany for the past 50 years," she said.

The government is currently in final deliberations over its 2027 budget; spending upwards of €555 billion ($615 billion) is planned. Because revenue won't be enough to cover it, the government is planning to take on more than €118 billion in new debt. Adding the debt-financed special funds for infrastructure and the military, the new borrowing adds up to almost €204 billion.
Could Germany lose its top rating?

The economic experts have warned that if Germany continues with this path, the debt-to-GDP ratio could rise to 100% by 2040. This ratio indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it was 63.5%.

Germany is the only country of the world's leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) to still hold a AAA rating, the best possible credit rating in finance markets. It signals to investors the smallest possible default risk for German government bonds. "I want it to stay that way," Merz emphasized.
Germany under pressure

However, taking on less debt will not be simple. "A reduction in debt-based financing presents policymakers with a consolidation task of historic proportions and will require tough decisions," said Schnitzer. The belt-tightening must, however, be designed to enable growth. Some recommendations include reducing environmentally harmful tax benefits — like the energy tax breaks for diesel fuel.
The so-called "mothers' pension", a pension subsidy for older parents, should be revoked, said the experts. Tax increases could become necessary in the medium term, for example with value-added tax.
"The burden should be shared fairly between generations and societal groups," Schnitzer said.
Merz wants austerity throughout Europe

According to the chancellor, the experts' message has been received. Solid state finances are an issue in Germany but also throughout the European Union. Merz said there needs to be a consolidation course, adding that politicians have a duty to the younger generation. Reforms are needed, especially when it comes to social security systems.
Young startups — Germany's next tech champions?

Economic researchers are setting their hopes on increasing companies' productivity. Put simply, productivity describes how much a company can generate with its employees, machinery and resources in a set time.
According to the Council of Economic Experts, there is enormous variation even within the same industries. In Germany, the top companies are up to five times as productive as the weakest enterprises.

If the less productive companies caught up, economic growth could increase significantly, it said in the report. "New technologies and business models could drive peak productivity and allow new highly productive companies to develop."
Germany needs startups, venture capital
But innovations need capital. It's here that the Ifo Economic Research Institute sees considerable deficiencies.

New evaluations show that German universities produce significantly fewer successful business startups than their counterparts in the United Kingdom or United States. For example, for every 1,000 students, about 14 venture capital-backed founders emerge from the vicinity of Stanford University each year. In Cambridge, the European leader, it's 3.5. In Munich, by contrast, it's only 0.5.

There continues to be an abundance of inventors and tinkerers in Germany, especially in mechanical engineering. However, the message from the industry summit in Berlin was that for renewed success, labor costs must come down. Suggestions included longer working hours and more flexibility for employers around job protection.

The intention was not to cut employees' wages and salaries. However, a new study by the German Economic Institute commissioned for the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association showed that extending the working week by an hour alone would increase real gross domestic product by 1.5% in the coming five years.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: DA accelerates ASF vaccination; 65 percent of areas recovered
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) has vaccinated nearly half a million pigs against African swine fever (ASF), while 65 percent of previously affected areas have recovered, marking progress in…

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am
Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said the government must step up vaccination to support its hog repopulation program and restore domestic swine production to pre-ASF levels.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Agriculture (DA) has vaccinated nearly half a million pigs against African swine fever (ASF), while 65 percent of previously affected areas have recovered, marking progress in efforts to rebuild the country’s hog industry after seven years of recurring outbreaks.

“Vaccination must move faster and reach more farms if we are to make our repopulation program work. The goal is not just to contain ASF, but to rebuild the swine industry to where it was before the disease struck,” Tiu Laurel said.
Despite recent growth in the hog industry, the country’s swine population remains well below the approximately 13 million heads recorded in 2019, before ASF began devastating local farms.

Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI) director Christian Daquigan reported the DA had administered 499,008 of the 500,000 doses available under its ASF vaccination program from 2024 up to the first half of 2026, equivalent to 99.8 percent utilization.
The campaign covered 54 farms across seven provinces, including 29 commercial operations, 13 semi-commercial farms, 11 smallholder facilities and one government-owned operation.
Tarlac accounted for the largest number of vaccinated pigs at 287,620, followed by Batangas with 92,021 and Bulacan with 88,107. Other covered provinces were Rizal, Laguna, Quezon and Pampanga.
The vaccination effort gained headway on Aug. 27, when the BAI registered Vietnam’s AVAC ASF live vaccine for commercialization in the Philippines.
The agency said vaccination would complement established disease prevention and control measures.
The DA is also strengthening protection at the community level, particularly among backyard hog raisers, through its Community Animal Biosecurity Interventions program.
As of Oct. 22, active infections have remained in 236 barangays across 23 provinces.
However, 716 cities and municipalities have been reclassified as buffer or surveillance zones, accounting for 64.68 percent of previously affected areas.

articles.title: Canada provides $26 million aid for Philippines projects
articles.summary: Canada is giving $26 million in assistance to the Philippines for projects that will support community resilience, investment readiness and food logistics in the Luzon Economic Corridor.

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Canada is giving $26 million in assistance to the Philippines for projects that will support community resilience, investment readiness and food logistics in the Luzon Economic Corridor.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney made the announcement on Saturday, which will also support climate-resilient agriculture and the strengthening of nuclear regulatory capacity in the Philippines.
Carney underscored Canada’s commitment to supporting the Philippines’ long-term prosperity and resilience, as he met with President Marcos over the weekend.
Carney and Marcos highlighted the significant expansion of cooperation under the Canada-Philippines Strategic Partnership across trade, development, energy and people-to-people ties.

With bilateral merchandise trade reaching $3.4 billion in 2025, the leaders welcomed the successful conclusion of negotiations for a Canada-Philippines free trade agreement, just one year after they announced its launch.
Both countries are now working toward the agreement’s signature in 2027. Once in force, this agreement could increase exports up to three times by 2035.
The leaders also emphasized efforts to advance defense and security cooperation, including the implementation of the Status of Visiting Forces Agreement.

New joint measures to improve information sharing and strengthen border and cybersecurity were also outlined, including the launch of a new cybersecurity dialogue, increased military cooperation through biannual military-to-military talks and steps toward agreements on customs cooperation and the protection of sensitive information.

Marcos and Carney exchanged views on regional issues and reaffirmed their shared commitment to a free, open, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific. They agreed to continue advancing cooperation on shared priorities, including economic growth, security, infrastructure development and food security.
Satellite surveillance cooperation

Canada also announced the extension of its Dark Vessel Detection Program in the Philippines that is expected to heighten the country’s maritime domain awareness and unreported fishing within its waters.

Philippine Ambassador to Canada Jose Victor Chan Gonzaga said the extension shows the strong partnership between the Philippines and Canada in combatting illegal unreported and unregulated fishing activities.
Canada signed in 2023 a five-year agreement with the Philippines to provide its Dark Vessel Detection system.

articles.title: ‘Government has only until December 2 to collect Marcoses’ estate tax’
articles.summary: The 1Sambayan coalition has called on newly appointed Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Commissioner Rolando Ligon Jr. to take immediate steps to ensure collection of the Marcos family’s unpaid…

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The 1Sambayan coalition has called on newly appointed Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Commissioner Rolando Ligon Jr. to take immediate steps to ensure collection of the Marcos family’s unpaid estate.
In a statement, the group said the government faces a “critical deadline” on Dec. 2, as it marks five years since the BIR issued its nd on the Marcos heirs in 2021.

Ligon was urged by 1Sambayan to act promptly and if legally required, issue and ensure the proper service and receipt of the necessary demand on the Marcos heirs before the applicable prescription period expires.
“This is not a matter of political preference. It is a matter of enforcing a final and executory judgment and protecting government revenues that belong to the Filipino people,” it said.
The estate was assessed at P23 billion in taxes in 1991, with the Supreme Court subsequently affirming the assessment.
The ruling became final and executory in 1999. With accumulated interest and penalties, the liability has grown to approximately P203 billion as of December 2021.
“This is not merely a private family obligation. It is a public claim – money legally due (to) the Filipino people,” 1Sambayan said.

The group explained that the government is subject to rules on the prescription of tax collection, including the requirement that collection efforts be undertaken within the applicable period, under the Tax Code.
If the government’s right to collect is indeed to be preserved by a renewed written demand, that demand must be made within the prescribed period, it said.
The group said the government has a responsibility to pursue the lawful collection of tax liabilities that have been judicially affirmed with finality.
“Failure to take the necessary steps within the period prescribed by law could result in the loss of public revenue and raise serious questions of accountability,” 1Sambayan said.
The group noted that Ligon serves under the President who is himself an heir and co-administrator of the Marcos estate.

“That circumstance makes the BIR’s actions all the more important – not because the Commissioner should be presumed to be conflicted, but because public confidence requires that the law be seen to operate equally, regardless of the identity or political power of the taxpayer,” 1Sambayan said.

articles.title: Defense witnesses’ ties to Dutertes questioned
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has questioned the credibility of the witnesses presented by the defense team, saying their personal and…

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte (front R) leaves court after posting bail in Quezon City, suburban Manila on September 5, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution panel in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has questioned the credibility of the witnesses presented by the defense team, saying their personal and professional ties to her family raise doubts about their impartiality.
“All of them are biased, that’s why their credibility was tested in court,” House prosecution spokesman Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said in an interview over Bilyonaryo News Channel.
He said many of the defense witnesses were either former government appointees, business associates or longtime friends of Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio.
Among those he was referring to were Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin, lawyers Suzette Balucanag-Punay and Anel Martin Antero, and Chadwin Parian.
Adalin, who served under then Davao City mayor Duterte, testified about a property registered under Carpio that the prosecution had questioned as allegedly undeclared.

Punay, the in-house counsel of GenCorp Industries Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corp., testified about Duterte’s business interests and monthly payments she received from GenCorp’s Times Square branch.

Antero, a longtime friend of Duterte, appeared before the impeachment court to explain a P205,000 dinner in Japan, while Parian, a friend of Carpio, testified about a P256,882 Nike purchase in Malaysia.

Adiong observed that the backgrounds of the defense witnesses were very much different from the prosecution’s witnesses, which included government officials and custodians of official financial and corporate records.
He said those officials testified primarily based on documents submitted to their agencies rather than on personal relationships with the Vice President.
He added that some defense witnesses appeared evasive when confronted with difficult questions from senator-judges, invoking ignorance or forgetfulness.
“When they are hard-pressed with questions by the senators, their sanctuary to evade these are ‘I don’t know, I can’t recall, I can’t remember,’” he said.
Adiong maintained that witnesses should answer questions candidly and transparently rather than selectively disclose only information favorable to the defense.

House Assistant Majority Leader Rep. Jude Acidre said senators should examine the relationship of each witness to the parties while assessing how their testimony compares with the documents presented by government agencies and financial institutions.

“If we will compare the witnesses of the prosecution and the defense, we can see that the ones who will not benefit from their testimony, have no personal interest or connection to the one in trial are more credible,” he said.
The defense began presenting its evidence on Nov. 9 to challenge the prosecution’s findings of at least P817.87 million in Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth.
The Senate impeachment court is scheduled to resume hearings on Nov. 19 and 20.

articles.title: Philippines, Australia forge updated defense cooperation
articles.summary: The Philippines and Australia have signed an updated defense cooperation agreement, aimed at expanding joint activities and strengthening the country’s military deterrence.

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and Australian Ambassador Marc Innes-Brown signed the Philippines-Australia Defense Cooperation Arrangement (DCA) at the Manila South Harbor yesterday.
Department of National Defense - Philippines / Facebook page
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Australia have signed an updated defense cooperation agreement, aimed at expanding joint activities and strengthening the country’s military deterrence.

The Department of National Defense said the new DCA provides a basis for further enhancement of defense engagements and cooperation in areas of mutual interest, building on 30 years of implementation of the 1995 DCA between the two countries.

“(The) stance in the West Philippine Sea of the President is that all entitlements are Philippine entitlements. It will bolster our credible deterrence posture in areas where we have jurisdiction,” Teodoro told reporters.

The agreement, according to Teodoro, is a mechanism that would make possible more joint maritime, air and land activities between the two countries under the Philippines-Australia Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA).

“It will make things much, much faster and easier. Rather than 100 steps to do a single thing, it will just now take 10 and it will be more purposive and not ad hoc,” Teodoro said. “It is the anti-red tape measure of our SOVFA.”
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, who is in Manila for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit, witnessed the signing of the DCA.
“And today with the signing of the Defense Cooperation Agreement, we’re taking that even further. Because building stronger ties with our neighbors makes Australia safer,” Albanese wrote on X.
The DCA also builds on the Statement of Intent on Enhanced Defense Cooperation signed by Teodoro and Australian Minister for Defense Richard Marles on Aug. 22 last year.

The statement recognized the need for an updated framework that reflects the breadth, depth and growing importance of defense cooperation between the two countries amid an increasingly complex regional security environment.
The agreement’s signing also coincides with the 80th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the Philippines and Australia.

articles.title: ‘Leverage Asean meet for investments, jobs’
articles.summary: As the Philippines hosts the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, Sen. Mark Villar is urging the government to leverage the event to secure new investments, generate jobs and…

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. joins fellow Southeast Asian leaders and youth delegates during the opening of the ASEAN Leaders' Interface with Representatives of ASEAN Youth at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City on November 15, 2026.
PPA Pool Photos by Niño Jesus Orbeta

MANILA, Philippines — As the Philippines hosts the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, Sen. Mark Villar is urging the government to leverage the event to secure new investments, generate jobs and cushion the impact of rising inflation on Filipinos.

Villar emphasized that the country’s leadership in the regional bloc must translate into tangible economic benefits for citizens currently grappling with high electricity costs and rising prices of basic commodities.
The call comes against the backdrop of recent Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) data showing inflation accelerating to 7.8 percent in October.

Transport inflation also surged to 20.1 percent, while rice inflation climbed to 20.7 percent. Additionally, the September Labor Force Survey recorded 2.86 million unemployed and 5.56 million underemployed Filipinos.
Villar noted that the ASEAN region, with a combined economy of $3.9 trillion and a population of nearly 700 million, offers massive opportunities for trade and business expansion.

Meanwhile, Sen. Erwin Tulfo said a Belgian firm has expressed interest in constructing an oil refinery and depot in the Philippines at no cost to the government, a move that could help secure the country’s fuel supply amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

In a letter sent to the Senate committee on energy, Brightside Industries Group has proposed building the facilities, mirroring an earlier initiative floated by the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company of the United Arab Emirates.

“The more companies that will build oil depot and refinery in the Philippines, the better. Because we can ensure that when there’s conflict in the Middle East, we will still have enough supply,” Tulfo, who chairs the energy committee, said.

He explained that under the proposed arrangement, the Philippines will not be required to shell out public funds. He surmised that the Belgian firm intends to use the country as a strategic storage hub to distribute and sell oil to other Asian markets.

articles.title: DMW: 17 Pinoy seafarers safe in US ship collision
articles.summary: All 17 Filipino crewmembers of a tanker carrying asphalt, which figured in a collision with a passenger riverboat on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans in Louisiana have been reported…

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am
A tugboat stabilizes cruise ship American Heritage after it capsized following a collision with a tanker on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, Louisiana on Nov. 13.

MANILA, Philippines — All 17 Filipino crewmembers of a tanker carrying asphalt, which figured in a collision with a passenger riverboat on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans in Louisiana have been reported safe.

The Department of Migrant Workers said the 17 Filipino crew members of the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Atlantic Asphalt have been accounted for following the accident which also involved American Cruise Lines vessel American Heritage on Nov. 13.
The DMW, through its Bagong Bayani Monitoring and Situation Room, is coordinating with the concerned parties to ensure the seafarers’ welfare.

“Preliminary reports indicate that the tanker may have experienced steering or maneuvering difficulties before the collision, prompting emergency responders to immediately conduct rescue and medical assistance operations,” the agency stated.
“Verification with the Local Manning Agency confirmed that all 17 Filipino crew members aboard the Atlantic Asphalt are accounted for and safe,” it added.
The local manning agency has confirmed the safety of the Filipino crew and is coordinating the submission of their individual details to the DMW for documentation and continued monitoring.
The United States Coast Guard and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the circumstances surrounding the collision.
The DMW said it would continue to monitor developments and coordinate with relevant authorities and agencies to ensure the safety and welfare of the Filipino seafarers.

articles.title: New Asean flag, emblem launched
articles.summary: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) launched yesterday its updated flag and emblem to reflect the official admission of Timor-Leste to the regional bloc.

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) launched yesterday its updated flag and emblem to reflect the official admission of Timor-Leste to the regional bloc.
The updated flag features 11 rice stalks inside a red-and-white circle on a blue field, symbolizing the expansion of the bloc to 11 member states.

“This year, the Cebu Protocol marked another step in that journey, reflecting an ASEAN of 11 that has shaped the future together,” President Marcos said in his remarks during the opening ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay.

The Cebu Protocol, adopted during the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu in May, formally added Timor-Leste as ASEAN’s 11th member and replaced the official ASEAN flag and emblem with updated versions. This was the first-ever change in the ASEAN Charter since its 2007 signing.

Marcos and First Lady Liza Marcos welcomed the leaders of ASEAN during the opening ceremony: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Thailand Prime Minister Anutin Charnivarakul, Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto, Vietnam Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, Lao PDR Prime Minister Saleuxmay Kommasith and Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão.
Also welcomed were Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister Hangchuon Naron and Mayanmar representative Director General U Han Win Aung.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Brazil President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and International Monetary Fund managing director Kristalina Georgieva also attended the opening ceremony.
Gusmão was seen dancing with Filipino performers during the opening ceremony to the tune of “Sama-sama Tayo,” a song composed for the Philippines’ hosting of ASEAN this year.
Marcos and other leaders were also seen riding colorful and custom-painted electric tricycles or e-trikes around the PICC.
The e-trikes have an “ASEAN” signage similar to those used by tricycles and jeepneys to indicate their routes.
The ASEAN-US Summit, which will be attended by United States President Donald Trump, is to take place tomorrow after the closing ceremony.

articles.title: President Marcos invited to visit Brazil in 2027
articles.summary: President Marcos may visit Brazil next year upon an invitation from its leader President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, as part of an initiative to strengthen ties between the Philippines and the…

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am

President Marcos and First Lady Liza Marcos welcome Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and First Lady Rosângela da Silva at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City on November 14, 2026.
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos may visit Brazil next year upon an invitation from its leader President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, as part of an initiative to strengthen ties between the Philippines and the South American nation.
Lula made the announcement at a press conference on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Pasay City yesterday.
Palace press officer Claire Castro said Marcos has not yet formally accepted the invitation.
Lula, who was in the country for a state visit, said he invited Marcos to Brazil following their bilateral meeting on Saturday.

Advancing partnership in renewable energy and biofuels, livestock production and animal health, modern farming, education, science and technology, law enforcement and other fields directly benefiting Filipinos highlighted Marcos’ meeting with Lula.
Marcos also invited the Brazilian leader as guest of the chair at the ASEAN plenary yesterday.

In a statement on Saturday, the Presidential Communications Office said Lula invited Marcos to visit Brazil “with a large business delegation to help both countries identify further areas for trade, investment and economic growth.”
Castro, however, deferred to the Department of Foreign Affairs when asked to confirm whether Marcos has accepted Lula’s invitation.

articles.title: Toward a stronger and more prosperous Indo-Pacific, together
articles.summary: It is my great pleasure to visit Manila and Shenzhen to attend the ASEAN-related Summit Meetings and the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. I wish to express my respect for the leadership…
articles.byline: Takaichi Sanae Prime Minister of Japan

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — It is my great pleasure to visit Manila and Shenzhen to attend the ASEAN-related Summit Meetings and the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. I wish to express my respect for the leadership demonstrated by both chairs.
A year ago, when I attended these two meetings just after assuming the office of Prime Minister, I received a warm welcome from the leaders of participating countries.

Since then, I have deepened ties with leaders from many countries, including through the state visit to Japan by President Marcos on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of the normalization of diplomatic relations between Japan and the Philippines.

As the free and open international order based on the rule of law faces a wide range of challenges and uncertainty in the global economy is increasing, leaders in the Indo-Pacific must engage in candid discussions and work together to address pressing issues.

As we mark the tenth anniversary of Japan’s vision of a “Free and Open Indo-Pacific” (FOIP) this year, in May, I have announced an “updated FOIP.” Japan will work with friends across the region to help each country acquire the freedom and resilience needed to determine its own future, so that the region as a whole can “grow stronger and become more resilient and prosperous together.”

One concrete area within this effort is ensuring a stable energy supply and strengthening supply chains. Japan launched “POWERR Asia,” a cooperative framework to broadly strengthen energy resilience, focusing on Asia, the region most heavily affected by the situation in the Middle East. In addition to supporting near-term procurement of crude oil and petroleum products in Asia, the initiative supports the development of stockpiling systems and the stable securing of energy sources. Japan intends to further strengthen this initiative by expanding its economic-resilience components to address regional needs.

ASEAN has also set out the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP), emphasizing fundamental principles shared with the FOIP, including openness, transparency, inclusiveness, and the rule of law. At last year’s ASEAN-Japan Summit, we issued a Joint Statement on the Further Promotion and Implementation of the AOIP and have advanced our cooperation. I am encouraged that ASEAN countries have recognized the alignment between the updated FOIP and the AOIP. At this year’s Summit, we intend to adopt a Joint Statement focused on economic resilience and further enhance synergies between the FOIP and AOIP.

The Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) Summit will also be held in Manila. To simultaneously achieve economic growth, decarbonization, and energy security, I intend to evolve AZEC into “AZEC 2.0,” with a stronger focus on economic and energy resilience.

The year 2027, when ASEAN, the linchpin of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific, marks the 60th anniversary of its founding, is fast approaching. It also coincides with the 50th anniversary of the announcement of Japan’s Three Principles toward Southeast Asia (known as the Fukuda Doctrine), which laid the foundation for Japan and ASEAN to move forward as equal partners connected “heart to heart.” Building on this half-century history, Japan will deepen Japan-ASEAN cooperation while respecting ASEAN Centrality and unity.

At the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting, in light of growing uncertainty in the global economy, I look forward to participating in discussions under China’s chairmanship on realizing a region in which everyone can enjoy the benefits of growth and prosperity. Looking ahead to 2031, Japan will chair APEC. Japan will further promote cooperation that responds to the challenges of the times, including promoting free and fair trade and investment based on rules, which Japan has long championed, and advancing WTO reform, as well as development of quality infrastructure and support for small and medium-sized enterprises. We will also further promote cooperation in the use of AI and digital technologies, energy security, and the development of resilient supply chains.

Since the end of World War II, Japan has consistently pursued its path as a peace-loving nation, and this stance will not change. At the end of this year, Japan plans to revise its Three Strategic Documents, including the National Security Strategy. Japan will continue contributing to the peace, stability, and prosperity of the international community in cooperation with countries including allies and like-minded countries.

I believe that the surest path toward realizing a “Free and Open Indo-Pacific” is for Japan and countries in the region to become more resilient and prosperous together through cooperation built up over the years. Japan will continue working with like-minded partners in the region to shape an Indo-Pacific that serves as a foundation for peace and prosperity in the international community.

articles.title: Two planes collide on taxiway at Miami airport one day after national grounding
articles.summary:
Two people injured after wingtip of Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck nose of United Parcel Service Boeing 767

Two planes collided with one another on a taxiway at Miami’s international…

blocks.text: Two planes collided with one another on a taxiway at Miami’s international airport on Saturday night – a day after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued an hours-long nationwide ground stop due to communication issues affecting multiple air traffic control centers.

In a statement, the Trump administration-led FAA said the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a United Parcel Service Boeing 767 “while the airplanes were taxiing at Miami International Airport”.
Two people reportedly had minor injuries in the collision and subsequently received medical treatment.
The FAA said it was investigating the matter, which was reported at about 9pm local time.

According to the FAA, air traffic controllers had told the UPS crew to give way to the Copa flight before the collision. “The Copa flight was taxiing to the gate and the UPS flight was taxiing for departure to Bogotá, Colombia,” the FAA said.
A passenger on the Copa flight, Cesar Ferreira, spoke to CNN about how screams from those around him clued him in to the emergency.

“We were taxiing after landing at a normal speed when, all of a sudden, I heard the chatter around me getting louder – followed by a collective scream and then the impact of another aircraft hitting ours,” Ferreira said. “Inside the cabin, we felt the plane jerk abruptly sideways. At first, some passengers started freaking out, but the Copa crew reacted quickly, getting everyone to remain seated.”
Copa Airlines said in a statement that it “regrets the disruption this incident may cause our passengers”.
“The safety of our passengers and crew is our top priority, and we will cooperate with authorities as they investigate,” the airline said.
The airport said flights were directed to other taxiways, so airport operations were not affected.

“We are aware of an incident involving one of our aircraft on the ground in Miami,” UPS said in a statement. “Our crew is safe, and we are committed to working with authorities to determine what happened. The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority.”

The weekend was marked by thousands of flight delays and cancelations in the wake of a four-hour FAA ground stop on Friday which the Trump administration said stemmed from routine but botched maintenance aiming to switch telecommunication lines from old copper wire to fiber optic cables.

Trump administration transportation secretary Sean Duffy on Saturday and Sunday blamed the need for the maintenance on a lack of congressional funding – though critics have said the White House has not spent the money it has been apportioned to upgrade the infrastructure supporting the US’s air travel system.

articles.title: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony full of emotions as Phil Collins, Queen Latifah, more inducted
articles.summary: Saturday night's Rock & Roll Hall of Came ceremony brought out stars and emotional tributes as Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Luther Vandross, Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte, Sade, Joy…

image.caption: Aerosmith joined Run DMC for the surprise closing performance of their classic collaboration, Walk This Way, on Saturday at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Saturday night's Rock & Roll Hall of Came ceremony brought out stars and emotional tributes as Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Luther Vandross, Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte, Sade, Joy Division/New Order and Iron Maiden were inducted during the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, along with producer Rick Rubin.
Run DMC and Aerosmith were surprise event closers, as Wu-Tang Clan, Rick Rubin, Iron Maiden, others inducted
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Nov 15, 2026 10:34 AM EST | Last Updated: 26 minutes ago

Phil Collins gave a tearful acceptance speech and got an electrifying tribute from Cynthia Erivo, Oprah Winfrey inducted the late Luther Vandross, the crowd yelled along with Billy Idol, and Wu-Tang Clan crowded the stage for a rowdy celebration at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night.

Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte, Sade, Joy Division/New Order and Iron Maiden were also inducted during the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, along with producer Rick Rubin, who got a long-bearded tribute from the Red Hot Chili Peppers.
A night that beforehand felt like it might fall flat with the absences of key inductees was as lively and overloaded as the induction ceremony ever is.

U2 was the night's surprise opener, playing their new single Silencio while surrounded by dancers in riot squad gear. They then launched into their 1984 classic Pride (In the Name of Love) as singer Bono alternately raised a peace sign and fist.
Run DMC and Aerosmith were the surprise closers with a loud jam of Walk This Way, their 1986 classic collaboration, produced by Rubin.
Queen Latifah, left, and Megan Thee Stallion perform during the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony on Saturday in Los Angeles. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)
Collins gets emotional, Idol gets wild

The 75-year-old Collins, whose mobility trouble and other health problems kept him from performing, took the stage slowly using a pair of canes and cried at a huge ovation from a crowd that included his daughter, actor Lily Collins, and four other children.

items: Queen Latifah, Billy Idol, Sade and Oasis among artists being inducted into Rock & Roll Hall of Fame

blocks.text: Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker inducted Collins and praised him for his unprecedented dual stardom as a drummer and a hit-making pop singer in the 1980s.
"I grew up just wanting to play the drums," Collins said. "Everything else has been a really happy accident. I can't believe, when I look back, how life has gone."
Phil Collins, left, is introduced by Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker during Saturday's ceremony, before Collins shared a tearful speech. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)
Collins was already in the hall as a member of Genesis, but now gets the solo honour.
Hours later, the crowd leapt to its feet and shouted along with White Wedding during the induction of Idol — one of the few artists ticket buyers knew for sure would show up and perform.
He was inducted along with his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens by No Doubt members Gwen Stefani and Tony Kanal, who joined Idol for a duet on Eyes Without a Face.
Oprah inducts Luther Vandross
Winfrey said with relish that Vandross was "the maestro of the love song" and said he was once correctly named "the top artist that people make love to."
Vandross, an R&B singer with a velvet voice, was one of the definitive singers of the 1980s and '90s. He died in 2005.
"Luther Vandross sang with such passion and soul it could reach something deep inside that you didn’t even know needed to be reached," Winfrey said.
Hip-hop acts make their presence known

Wu-Tang Clan, the hip-hop collective from New York's Staten Island, filled the stage with its 10 current members, giving a memorable acceptance speech and a performance that had the crowd on its feet dancing. Backed by a big jazz band, the musical medley included C.R.E.A.M., Method Man and late member Ol' Dirty Bastard's Shimmy Shimmy Ya.
"Wu-Tang rewrote the rules of hip-hop and did it without a big machine behind them," said comedian Chris Rock, who inducted them.
Audience members put up Wu-Tang Clan hand signs as the Wu-Tang Clan performs during the ceremony on Saturday. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)

MC Lyte, a trailblazing female rapper starting in the late 1980s, was the first artist inducted, with hip-hop star Remy Ma doing the honours. Her contemporary and fellow groundbreaker Latifah was inducted later in the evening by Megan Thee Stallion, who said Latifah "taught us to recognize royalty within ourselves."
Latifah said that for a long time, she would not have believed this night was possible.
"It's difficult enough being a woman in hip-hop," she said, "let alone being a hip-hopper in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame."
Inductee Queen Latifah speaks during the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday in L.A. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)
Latifah and MC Lyte then took the stage together to perform a medley of their hits, including Latifah's U.N.I.T.Y. and MC Lyte's Ruffneck.
They entered the hall as recipients of the Early Influence Award along with posthumous inductees Gram Parsons, Fela Kuti and Celia Cruz, who were all inducted via video tribute.
A stage full of Rick Rubins
Legendary rock, hip-hop and country producer Rubin accepted his induction with a one-sentence acceptance speech.
"You can't kill rock 'n' roll," he said, and left the stage.
The Red Hot Chili Peppers dressed as Rick Rubin during their performance at the ceremony on Saturday. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)

The Red Hot Chili Peppers then appeared, all four of them wearing white wigs and long white fake beards to match Rubin's signature look as they played their 1991 breakthrough hit Give It Away, one of many he produced for them.
Oasis and the other no-shows
Oasis, the youngest of the inductees, didn’t show up. Guitarist Noel Gallagher was playing a gig back home in Britain, and his younger brother, Liam Gallagher, has said he just didn't want to come.
"Anybody surprised they didn’t show up?" asked actor and Oasis superfan Bob Odenkirk, who inducted them. "It would’ve been out of character if they had. I would've been worried."

items: It's time to revisit Sade's legacy

blocks.text: Iron Maiden, the quintessential British heavy metal band of the 1980s, as well as iconic singer Sade weren't at the event. Joy Division and New Order got a joint induction, with only the bassist for both bands, Peter Hook, showing up at the ceremony.
After streaming the ceremony live for the past few years, the hall returned to its previous format, where the public won't see it until an edited version airs on ABC and Disney+ on Dec. 9.

articles.title: Pope Leo heads to high Andes on final leg of South America tour
articles.summary: Leo, originally from Chicago, served as the bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 until 2023. He is expected to spotlight Indigenous rights and environmental protection on the final leg of his tour.

image.caption: Pope Leo earlier visited Zana, a center of Afro-Peruvian cultureImage: Andrew Medichini/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV arrived in the Andes Mountains of Peru on Sunday for the final leg of his South American tour.
The pontiff, who served in Peru for 20 years, was expected to spotlight Indigenous rights and Amazon protection during his remaining engagements.
Leo arrived on Sunday in Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire that sits at an altitude of 3,400 meters (more than 11,000 feet).
Peruvian Cardinal Pedro Barreto told the Associated Press that "Leo is clearing the path laid out" by his predecessor, Pope France, on environmental protection and human rights.

blocks.caption: Thousands of faithful lined the cobblestone streets of Cusco on Sunday awaiting the Pope's visitImage: Jose Sotomayor/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Next, we will travel to Pucallpa, a city in the Amazon that faces joint threats from deforestation and illegal mining.

"For us, the pope's arrival is a source of great joy, but it is also a great ​opportunity to make our demands, ‌our grievances, and our problems heard," said Cecilio Soria, an Indigenous human rights activist.
Pope acknowledges suffering, contributions of Afro-Peruvians
Earlier, on Saturday, Leo held an open-air Mass in town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba.

He spoke with pleasure of returning to the "steep hills, ravines and fertile valleys, in a land with Andean roots, where the Inca Empire flourished and which is the cradle of a profound Christian faith."

blocks.caption: Pope Leo held Mass in the small town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, located in his former Diocese of ChiclayoImage: Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media/ABACA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Leo also visited the city of Zana, some 45 kilometers (28 miles) southeast, which is a major center of Afro-Peruvian society.
Leo, who apologized for the Church's role in transatlantic slavery in May. said Zana "preserves the memory of generations of Africans who were torn from their homes and subjected to slavery."

blocks.caption: Thousands have flocked to Leo's open-air Masses around PeruImage: Silvia Izquierdo/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: "Many endured great suffering and humiliation. Dear brothers and sisters of African descent, today I want to express my affection and closeness to you," he said.
"Thank you for all that you contribute to the life of this church."
Leo laments instability, violence in Peru
Leo, originally from Chicago, served as the bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 until 2023, when he was called to the Vatican. He holds both US and Peruvian citizenship.
For both Leo and the city's faithful, his stop in Chiclayo marked an emotional homecoming.

blocks.caption: The pope received a warm welcome in ZanaImage: Rodrigo Abd/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Speaking from his former cathedral, he addressed growing unrest and political instability a country where the homicide rate has doubled over the past five years and far-right President Keiko Fujimori was elected after promising to tackle crime.

"We feel threatened by the uncertainty of widespread violence and by the unspeakable suffering that continues to afflict so many of our brothers and sisters," Leo said at the Cathedral of St. Mary in Chiclayo on Saturday.
"Yet, despite this darkness, which so often dims our hope and weakens our trust, God's gift continues to shine before our eyes."

blocks.caption: Chiclayo, Leo's former home, served as a base for much of the Peru tourImage: Andrew Medichini/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Leo is scheduled to arrive in the Peruvian capital, Lima, on Sunday evening, before traveling back to Rome on Monday.

articles.title: Quebec Premier and PM Carney discuss U.S. trade, homelessness at first meeting in Cambodia
articles.summary: St-Pierre Plamondon said the meeting ended with federal support for the province's fight against homelessness, and the exchange of personal phone numbers. The premier also thanked the Prime Minister…

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon joke around at the start of their first meeting in Phnom Penh, Cambodia on Sunday. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Montreal

St-Pierre Plamondon said the meeting ended with federal support for the province's fight against homelessness, and the exchange of personal phone numbers. The premier also thanked the Prime Minister for his support of an economic summit that will take place in Quebec in 2027.
The premier said that the tone was "very agreeable" and that the two leaders "had fun"

Prime Minister Mark Carney and Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon met for the first time since the provincial election at the Francophonie Summit in Cambodia — a 30-minute meeting that St-Pierre Plamondon called "very agreeable, very funny."
"From a personal standpoint, I think it went well," said St-Pierre Plamondon in a news conference following the meeting. "We laughed on several occasions, we had fun."
The two men met at a hotel in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia, during the summit of the international body of French-speaking states and governments.
Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks at a summit event in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

The premier said that the meeting yielded tangible results, including federal support for the province's plan to tackle the homelessness crisis and the exchange of personal phone numbers to keep open lines of communication between the two.
The premier also celebrated Carney for helping to cement Quebec's deal to host an international economic summit in Quebec in 2027 that would help to diversify the province's trade.
He also said it was the first of many meetings they would have.

"What is evident for the two of us, I think, is that we share some of the same objectives," said Carney, emphasizing his desire to put an end to homelessness nationally and make life more affordable in all provinces.

St-Pierre Plamondon said that several issues were left outstanding that couldn't be tackled in their half hour meeting — namely: immigration, housing, the Alto high-speed rail project and a fulsome discussion on U.S. trade.
"We agreed that we needed to talk to each other on a regular basis," he said of how the province would collaborate with the federal government on U.S. relations.
"Historically, Quebec has been very active diplomatically in the U.S.. So we're going to do that."

When asked if the premier regretted the tone of his first interactions with the prime minister after being sworn in, where he accused Carney of muzzling him during an EU summit that took place in Montreal in October, St-Pierre Plamondon said: "I will never regret defending the interests of Quebec."

items: PQ accuses Ottawa of muzzling Quebec during upcoming Canada-EU summit
Quebec premier officially withdraws from Canada-EU summit, will send chief diplomat

blocks.text: The premier said that over the course of the summit, he has been treated by and considered as a head of state with other countries which has led to meetings which yielded fruitful results for Quebec's economy.
"The truth is here, we are treated as a full nation," he said. "That recognition leads us to very practical conversations about what we can do from an economic standpoint."
He explained that bilateral meetings he has had at the generated commerce for the next years with countries who want to diversify their economic structures.
"In terms of a first visit abroad, we're very happy."

articles.title: 'He lived and breathed it': NCAA football prospect from N.S. has died
articles.summary: A Nova Scotian who was set to play football at an American powerhouse college is being remembered for his exceptional talent and desire to get better on the field, but his happy-go-lucky and…

image.caption: Marcellus Young Casario, 18, had committed to attending the University of Georgia beginning next year and playing for the NCAA Division I football powerhouse. (University of Georgia)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New

A Nova Scotian who was set to play football at an American powerhouse college is being remembered for his exceptional talent and desire to get better on the field, but his happy-go-lucky and teddy-bear nature off of it.
Marcellus Young Casario, committed to Georgia Bulldogs, remembered for boundless energy, happy-go-lucky nature

A Nova Scotian who was set to play football at an American powerhouse college is being remembered for his exceptional talent and desire to get better on the field, but his happy-go-lucky and teddy-bear nature off it.

Marcellus Young Casario, 18, a Grade 12 student at a Georgia prep school, died Friday after a medical emergency. His father, Devin Casario, said his son hadn't been feeling well lately and had been experiencing some heart issues.

The six-foot-six, 275-pound defensive end who grew up in Halifax was set to graduate high school next month and begin attending the University of Georgia in January, a school that has produced many NFL stars.
"He lived and breathed it, and his work ethic was incredible," said Devin Casario. "He had [a] relentless motor and he was very, very coachable."
Former coaches say that while Casario's size, speed and strength were exceptional, his desire to get better is what made him stand out.
Marcellus Young Casario is shown in a photo from his time playing with Rabun Gap in Georgia. (Submitted by Devin Casario)
Chanuen Flint, a former coach and family friend, said that even at the age of six when Casario started playing football, his passion was evident.
"You just knew right away when he showed up on the field, he was all business. [He] had fun doing it, but he was there to play football," said Flint.
Early days

Colby Smith helped coach Casario when he played mites football, for kids who are seven and eight. He remembers the team playing in a halftime scrimmage at a Saint Mary's University football game. The children formed a tunnel to give the giant university players high-fives as they came out onto the field.
"I think from that very moment he knew where he wanted to be when he got older … I can remember the look on his face when they came out and he wanted to be part of that," said Smith.
Casario played minor football for teams in Halifax, Timberlea and the South Shore.
He left the province four years ago to attend a boarding school in Aurora, Ont., which played some of its games against American schools.
Marcellus Young Casario, shown wearing No. 50, always stood out for his size playing minor football in Nova Scotia. (Susanna Baard)
Marcello Lio, the head coach at St. Andrew's College, coached Casario for two years.

"Sometimes it’s easy for a young man, maybe not as passionate, to walk away from a loss, accept it and move on," said Lio. "He had struggled with that, so he always had the will to want to be better individually and want the team to win."
Overcoming adversity
Casario attended Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School, a Georgia prep school, for the past two years. He had a hip labrum injury last year that required surgery and a six-month recovery.
It wasn't clear whether he would return to full form.
In August, when training camp began, Devin Casario remembers getting a call from his son, who was in tears.

"I thought something had happened," said Devin Casario. "But there were tears of joy because I really think his self-belief and faith were tested after that recovery process. And I think after that first night during the conditioning test down there, he knew that he was going to be OK."
Marcellus Young Casario is shown in his senior class photo. (Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School/Facebook)
The University of Georgia wasn't Casario's only suitor. There were visits to Michigan State and Georgia Tech, all of which are well known for their football programs.
Lio said he wasn't surprised that Casario chose the University of Georgia. There were other schools where he might have been able to get on the field sooner, but the Bulldogs offered something else.
"He wanted to be pushed; there was some yearning inside him to be constantly pushed hard to be the best he can be," said Lio.
During the past two summers, when Casario returned to Nova Scotia when school was not in session, he helped coach Flint's younger son, who also plays defensive end.
Smith said Casario was always very respectful, continuing to call him "Coach" long after he was his coach.
"Even though he had these great accomplishments, he always remembered where he came from and always paid homage to all the people that helped him get where he is," said Smith.
Criminology studies
Devin Casario said his son planned to study criminology at the University of Georgia.
He said off the field, his son led a quiet life and his faith was very important to him.

"I hope something positive can come from this tragedy, and that he can serve as an inspiration to other athletes who have dreams, you know, coming out of Nova Scotia and the East Coast that through talent and hard work, perseverance, anything is possible," said Devin Casario.
"And, you know, our family is destroyed right now and trying to make sense of this, but we're so proud of him. And it's just so unfortunate that his life was cut short."
